title: Security Eng standup - vuln triage & secrets review (2026-03-18)
content:
Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Evelyn, Samir, Jamal (10:00-10:30)

Agenda:
- Quick standup updates
- Vulnerability triage: outstanding high/critical findings from weekly scan
- Secrets review: recent S3/CI leak detection alerts
- Threat modeling primer for Private deployment networking changes
- Action items and owners

1) Quick updates (2 mins each)
- Aisha: follow-ups on SEC-610 (dependency upgrade). Coordinating with platform-eng to schedule canary. Investigating Snyk false-positive on libcrypto. Blocking: need infra window for canary. ETA: Wed 2026-03-24 for schedule.
- Marcus: finished PoC for automated prefix KV-cache encryption check. Will push draft RFC this week. Also triaging the runtime kernel fuzz failures (related to quantized operator). Created RDW-3421 to track.
- Evelyn: led secrets alerts review overnight — 3 alerts across CI and one low-risk token in a test bucket. Rotations initiated. Need confirmation from solutions-eng on whether token was actually in use.
- Samir: audit logs ingestion flakiness still happening; raised a SRE ticket. Investigating role mappings between KMS and service accounts.
- Jamal: threat model prep for private deploy networking doc; will present first cut in next sync.

2) Vulnerability triage
- Summary of current scanner output (2026-03-17 nightly scan):
  - 2 Critical (CVE-2025-9999 in openssl on builder image; CVE-2026-0101 in third-party telemetry agent)
  - 4 High (various libs in analytics pipeline)
  - 7 Medium/Low

- Critical 1: CVE-2025-9999 (openssl) on builder/use-internal-images
  - Affected: build images used by CI -> potential supply-chain build compromise.
  - Evidence: image manifest shows vulnerable openssl:1.1.1k layer in 14% of builder images (containers/cicd-builder:v2026-02-10)
  - Risk: high for reproducible build tampering; exploit requires crafted TLS client server but possible in build-stage downloads.
  - Mitigation plan: rotate to patched builder base (openssl patched) and rebuild all official images.
  - Owner: Marcus Li (action: RDW-3421)
  - ETA: immediate patch to base by 2026-03-20, full image rebuild + CI smoke by 2026-03-24.
  - Temp control: block older builder tags in image registry; alert SRE to prevent new pipelines using old tag.

- Critical 2: CVE-2026-0101 (telemetry-agent) - untrusted deserialization vector
  - Affected: telemetry agent used in dedupe pipeline on Dedicated tenant infra.
  - Evidence: fuzz test reproduction on dev cluster; PoC confirmed deserialization with crafted payload.
  - Risk: remote code execution in telemetry pipeline; potential data leakage.
  - Mitigation: patch agent to latest upstream with hardened deserializer; if immediate patch not possible, disable telemetry ingestion for affected clusters and route to offline queue.
  - Owner: Samir Desai
  - ETA: disable ingestion by 2026-03-18 EOD, patch PR targeted for 2026-03-22.
  - Linked: GitHub PR in linked_artifacts.

- Highs: analytics deps (libxml2, thrift)
  - Approach: schedule dependency upgrades over 2-week window; prioritize runtime-exposed ones first.
  - Owner: Aisha + eng teams (multi-team coordination ticket SEC-679).

Notes: we decided NOT to change public-facing model-serving nodes for these two criticals today — risk vs customer impact judged. If telemetry agent remains unpatched after patch ETA, escalate to CTO.

3) Secrets review (alerts from secret-scanner, 2026-03-18 02:14)
- Alerts found: 4 alerts
  - 2 test tokens leaked in non-prod S3 buckets (public-read mistakenly applied)
    - Buckets: redwood-dev-artifacts/test-results, experiment-snapshots-temp
    - Remediation taken: buckets set to private, object ACLs adjusted, affected tokens rotated.
    - Owner: Evelyn Torres
    - Notes: tokens were expired but still rotated to be safe; documented in incident draft (Confluence link above).
  - 1 GitHub action secret printed to CI logs (masking failure)
    - Repo: infra/ops-scripts
    - Root cause: custom wrapper echoing debug env var in a try/catch path. Patch merged to remove debug echo.
    - Owner: Marcus Li
    - Action: rotate secret, update policy to fail builds when secrets are printed (policy: SEC-CI-03 enforcement).
  - 1 low-risk API key in a test fixture (not used in prod)
    - Decision: keep but mark as fixture-only and move to secrets manager with strict ACL; add test assertion to ensure keys are non-functional in prod.
    - Owner: Jamal

- CI/Policy improvement ideas from discussion:
  - Add a denylist for "public-read" ACLs on any bucket under redwood-* account in terraform plan checks (pre-apply hook).
  - Extend CI to scan for secrets in action logs (post-build) and fail fast.
  - Quick win: enable S3 object-level event that triggers a Lambda to auto-revoke any newly public objects and notify #sec-eng.
  - Owner for terraform pre-apply hook: Marcus (ETA 2026-03-31)

4) Threat modeling: Private deployment network changes
- Context: product wants to enable hybrid-private deployment where control plane remains in Redwood but data-plane can be customer-managed with peered VPCs.
- Presentation notes (Jamal): initial diagram reviewed (in Confluence). Primary threats discussed:
  - Data exfiltration via misconfigured peering or overly permissive security groups.
  - Control plane impersonation if TLS client auth not strict (man-in-the-middle risk during provisioning).
  - Insider threats: support tickets could be abused to request credentialed actions.
- Proposed mitigations:
  - Mutual TLS (mTLS) for control plane <-> data plane management traffic; require cert issued by Redwood CA opt-in per customer.
  - Strict egress rules on data-plane workers: deny outbound internet except to whitelisted endpoints (e.g., KMS, S3 endpoints) where necessary.
  - Request-for-action workflow: any credential change requested via support UI requires a two-person review and signed audit entry.
  - KMS integration: ensure keys live in customer's KMS where possible; fallback to Redwood KMS only with explicit consent.
- Open questions:
  - Operational cost of mTLS cert rotation for thousands of customers? (Jamal to estimate)
  - Telemetry/health checks over restricted egress: need design for proxying metrics through controlled endpoints.
- Action items:
  - Jamal: produce threat-modeling appendix describing threat matrix + mitigations by 2026-03-25.
  - Evelyn & Samir: prototype egress policy templates for common CSPs (AWS, GCP) by 2026-04-05.

5) Action items (summary)
- Marcus: block old builder images, implement registry tag deny, coordinate image rebuilds. Due 2026-03-24. Linked: RDW-3421. (owner)
- Samir: disable telemetry ingestion for affected clusters and PR patch to telemetry agent. Disable by 2026-03-18 EOD, patch by 2026-03-22.
- Aisha: coordinate analytics dep upgrades (SEC-679), schedule canary windows with platform-eng. Plan by 2026-03-20.
- Evelyn: finalize incident draft for secrets alerts and confirm rotations are complete. Due 2026-03-19.
- Jamal: threat-model appendix and plan for mTLS rotation cost estimate. Due 2026-03-25.
- Marcus: terraform pre-apply hook to prevent public-read buckets. Due 2026-03-31.

6) Risks / Escalations
- If telemetry agent patch is delayed beyond 2026-03-22 -> escalate to CTO and consider temporary customer-wide telemetry pause for Dedicated customers.
- If builder-image rebuilds slip past 2026-03-24 there is moderate risk of continued use of vulnerable images in CI; SRE enforced registry deny will be applied as temporary control.

7) Notes / artifacts to add after meeting
- Add incident draft to Confluence (Aisha/Evelyn)
- Create SEC-680 follow-up for automation of secrets rotation in CI and S3 event auto-remediation (Samir)
- Drop design sketches for mTLS rotation estimation into product-private-deploy page (Jamal)

Unresolved / parking-lot items:
- Formalize policy for customer KMS vs Redwood KMS for private deployments (lift to PM/Legal for contract language)
- Evaluate long-term telemetry agent replacement (are there lightweight alternatives?)

Meeting adjourned 10:32. Next sync (ad-hoc) once critical patches land or next weekly security sync Thursday 2026-03-25.

Notes-to-self: follow up in #sec-eng thread about automation runbooks; attach Snyk raw output for openssl finding to RDW-3421.
